name: brush
notes:
The vendored shell engine — brush, a bash-compatible shell written in Rust (MIT), the optional engine behind Mercury's Bash tool (settings `shellEngine` / MERCURY_SHELL_ENGINE=brush; the system bash stays the default). Pinned 2026-09-03 at the upstream release brush-shell-v0.4.0 (published 2026-05-03, the newest release at the pin). One upstream release archive per platform, flat: the `brush` binary, upstream's LICENSE and its THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.html (the crate notices of everything linked into the binary), both shipped whole beside the binary. Every sha256 is copied from upstream's own published `.sha256` asset (the `checksum` url), never computed locally; the fetch (bun run scripts/vendor/fetch-brush.ts) verifies the archive digest BEFORE extraction and installs the pack into vendor/brush// with its manifest — the host platform by default, --platform

/ --all for other caches. Linux pins the glibc (gnu) builds, the same family as the vendored Node runtime; upstream also publishes musl builds. No Windows entry: upstream publishes no Windows release binary, so the win-x64 pack is prepared on its own road and this lock does not pin it. Update procedure: bump version + tag, rewrite the four archive names, urls and checksum urls, copy each sha256 from the new release's .sha256 assets, run `bun run scripts/vendor/fetch-brush.ts --all`, rebuild, re-run `bash scripts/bash/run-all.sh`.
